speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome. I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with seizures, lethargy, and other neurological signs three days after birth; have you noticed any fever, poor feeding, or changes in your baby's skin color since delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is very concerning; given the history of chorioamnionitis and your low birth weight, I suspect a severe infection. Have you noticed any bulging of the soft spot on the top of the baby's head, and has the baby been passing stool or urine?

REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff, Blood_Culture, CRP, Glucose, Electrolytes, BUN, Creatinine, Total_Bilirubin.
REQUEST IMAGES: Cranial_Ultrasound.

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intraventricular Hemorrhage (Grade III or IV) secondary to Chorioamnionitis. The clinical picture of prematurity, sepsis (elevated CRP, low BP), and a tense fontanelle, combined with the ultrasound finding of ventricular bleeding, confirms this diagnosis.
